Article Title: 'Gang of dacoits': Yogi Adityanath says Akhilesh must apologise for UP 'loot and extortion'
Article Text:
Adityanath also revisited the issue of encephalitis, which he said had caused widespread fear in eastern Uttar Pradesh for decades.

Adityanath says UP has left 'BIMARU' image behind

CM attacks SP-Congress over encephalitis deaths

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday attacked the Samajwadi Party , calling it a "gang of dacoits" and accusing its leadership of looting the state exchequer during its tenure.Speaking in Deoria, he said SP president Akhilesh Yadav should apologise to the people of Uttar Pradesh over the alleged financial irregularities linked to the construction of the Jayaprakash Narayan International Centre (JPNIC) in Lucknow.Adityanath made the remarks while laying the foundation stones for 80 development projects worth more than Rs 305 crore in Deoria. He also contrasted the current state government with previous administrations, claiming that Uttar Pradesh had moved away from an image associated with poor governance, insecurity and the influence of criminal networks."SP means loot and extortion, SP means a gang of dacoits," Adityanath said.He directly targeted Akhilesh Yadav over the alleged misuse of public funds, saying, "For the loot of the state exchequer that the SP chief committed for his indulgence, he should apologise to the people," he said, referring to alleged corruption in the construction of the Jayaprakash Narayan International Centre (JPNIC) in Lucknow.The chief minister said Uttar Pradesh had previously been dominated by what he described as a "parallel government of mafias".He claimed the situation had changed under his administration, with criminal networks being dismantled and the state's image improving."Now UP has a good image. Mafias have been reduced to dust. Those who breach the security of daughters and traders have only two places to go -- they are either in jail or in hell," Adityanath said.He also linked development and governance to the election of "good public representatives", saying that the state's progress was a result of the choices made by voters."When good public representatives are elected, good governments come and the results are also good. This development, prosperity and employment are the result of the hard work of the public representatives whom you elected," he said.The chief minister said Uttar Pradesh had faced a severe deficit in development and public services before 2017."Before 2017, there was neither development nor security nor respect in Uttar Pradesh. There was no employment, nor houses, toilets, LPG connections, electricity and roads for the poor. Schools had become centres of cheating," he said.Adityanath also revisited the issue of encephalitis, which he said had caused widespread fear in eastern Uttar Pradesh for decades. He identified Deoria, Maharajganj, Gorakhpur, Siddharthnagar, Kushinagar, Sant Kabir Nagar and Basti among the districts that were particularly affected between July 15 and November 15 each year."This was not a disease; it was the sick mentality of the SP-Congress governments. In 40 years, 50,000 innocent children died, but no chief minister or prime minister from the SP or the Congress came to take stock of the situation," Adityanath said.The chief minister also invoked the term 'BIMARU', which was coined by demographer Ashish Bose in the mid-1980s to describe Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, then among India's poorest states.Adityanath said Uttar Pradesh had now moved beyond that description, pointing to improvements in development, security and infrastructure as evidence of the state's transformation.Agriculture minister Surya Pratap Shahi, minister of state for rural development Vijay Lakshmi Gautam, and MLAs Shalabh Mani Tripathi and Sabha Kunwar Kushwaha were among those present at the Deoria programme.
Article Summary: CM attacks SP-Congress over encephalitis deaths. Adityanath says UP has left 'BIMARU' image behind. CM attacks SP over alleged financial irregularities linked to the construction of the Jayaprakash Narayan International Centre in Lucknow.

Article Title: ‘Do you feel you are a lord?’ Bombay HC slams FDA, clears reopening of 5 eateries
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on slammed the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA), warning of contempt action against officials after the department refused to lift the suspension of food licences of five restaurants at the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) premises despite a fresh inspection finding them 88% compliant with food safety rules.“Tired of scolding the department and officers,” the division bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad said the FDA had taken a “pedantic instead of pragmatic view” despite the court’s earlier direction to reconsider the matter. The court ultimately vacated the suspension orders, allowing the five eateries at the MCA premises in Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC) to reopen.The MCA had challenged the FDA’s decision to suspend the restaurants’ licences over alleged hygiene violations and issues relating to third-party operations. A fresh inspection conducted on Thursday found the eateries to be 88% compliant with food safety requirements.However, the FDA had initially continued with the suspension, citing the fact that the restaurants were being operated by M/s Shirke Infrastructure, while the licences were registered in the MCA’s name.On Saturday, the FDA told the court that it would issue a fresh notice to the MCA, give it an opportunity to be heard on its contractual arrangement with Shirke Infrastructure and then pass a reasoned order.Accepting the undertaking, the court said the restaurants could reopen since the latest inspection had found them compliant. “There is no provision in the law that prohibits the same,” the bench observed.The court recalled that it had, during the previous hearing, specifically directed FDA officials to apply their minds and take a pragmatic approach to the licence issue.“However, despite clearly saying this, the FDA has disobeyed our order and taken a pedantic view instead of a pragmatic view. We are tired of scolding the department and officers all the time. It is now time to pass stinging orders. We will issue contempt action against the concerned officers. Let them convince us or go to jail," the court said.The bench also questioned why the FDA acted with “undue haste” without fully analysing the legal position.“How many times should we try to convince and balance equities so that the department does not feel discouraged? Why do we say don't kill a mosquito with a sword? Do you feel you are a lord and you can do anything?” HC questioned.The dispute began after the FDA suspended the five licences last week. At Tuesday’s hearing, the HC had praised FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe’s drive against hygiene lapses but asked the department to “be consistent” and “do it consistently and not in an ad hoc manner”.The court had ordered a fresh inspection while declining to stay the suspensions, though it allowed MCA to serve tea and coffee through vending machines as a temporary arrangement during ongoing tournaments.
Article Summary: The Bombay high court on slammed the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA), warning of contempt action against officials. The department refused to lift the suspension of food licences of five restaurants at the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) premises. The MCA had challenged the FDA’s decision to suspend the restaurants’ licences over alleged hygiene violations and issues relating to third-party operations.

Article Title: 'Suddhikaran another name for untouchability': Rahul Gandhi accuses BJP, RSS of discrimination against Kharge
Article Text:
Rahul alleges BJP of discriminatory politics

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Saturday attacked the Bharatiya Janata Party and Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh over a recent 'suddhikaran' or 'purification' ritual held at a venue in Uttarakhand where Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge had addressed a rally.Calling the practice "another name for untouchability", Rahul alleged that such an act was a crime under the Constitution.Addressing a presser at Congress headquarters in Delhi, the Rae Bareli MP said the country was witnessing a political contest between the ideology of the Constitution and that of the BJP and RSS."Our CLP leader in Rajasthan visits a temple, and BJP leaders perform a 'purification' ritual. Congress President Kharge ji, who has dedicated his entire life to the country and the Constitution, goes to the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani to deliver a speech, and a purification ritual is performed there. Who does this? It is the people from the BJP and RSS," Rahul said."Only BJP and RSS members do this, and it is a crime. Under India's Constitution, this is a crime, a criminal activity. 'Purification' is actually just another name for untouchability. Untouchability was outlawed, yet BJP members practice it openly," he added.Former Congress president said the ritual suggested that Dalits were "unclean" and should not be touched."When they perform this purification, they are effectively saying that Dalits should not be touched, that Dalits are unclean, and this constitutes a crime under the Indian Constitution," he said.Rahul also said the larger political contest in the country was between two opposing ideologies."A fight is under way in the country between two ideologies. On one side is the Constitution of India, the Constitution of Ambedkar, Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Patel. On the other is the ideology of the BJP and RSS. The politics currently playing out in India is between these two ideologies," Rahul said.He also spoke about alleged caste-based discrimination and said Dalits continue to face discrimination despite constitutional safeguards."For thousands of years, Dalits in this country have been subjected to atrocities and violence. While the Constitution made this illegal, even today, Dalit children in schools are made to clean toilets and sweep and mop floors," he said."Just think about the impact this has on the minds of the future generation: children see some of their peers sweeping, while those doing the sweeping see others who do not have to do so. This is the reality of India," he added.Congress leader further alleged that caste discrimination was also visible in access to common resources such as water."Dalits are not allowed to drink water from the village well; they have had to dig their own private wells because they were barred from using the common village well," Rahul claimed.He also alleged that caste discrimination could be seen at tea stalls."At tea stalls, you see two types of cups in use: a reusable glass cup that can be washed, and a paper or plastic cup that is discarded after use. The plastic or paper cups are for Dalits, while the glass ones are for others," he alleged."This is the reality of India. This is the reality of Uttar Pradesh, the reality of North India, and you can see this in cities and villages," Rahul added.The Haldwani controversy relates to a Congress rally held at Ramlila Maidan on August 8, ahead of the 2027 Uttarakhand assembly elections. Members of a right-wing group later performed a purification ritual at the venue, drawing criticism from Congress leaders.Kharge also raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha, linking the incident to his identity as a Dalit leader and alleging that it was an attempt to portray him as "untouchable".Kharge said he did not mention any community or religion during his speech at the venue."But after my speech, people associated with the BJP carried out a 'purification' ritual of that stage. You may have read about this in the newspapers. Is this the way things should happen in a democracy? How are you protecting the Constitution?" Kharge had said.He later took to X and said he did not want the incident to be politicised, while calling for strict legal action and demanding that a case be filed under the Untouchability Act against those who conducted the ritual.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi attacked the Bharatiya Janata Party and Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh over a recent 'purification' ritual held at a venue in Uttarakhand. Called the practice "another name for untouchability", Rahul alleged that such an act was a crime under the Constitution.

Article Title: 'Took off for Kathmandu blissfully unaware': Shashi Tharoor on deadly Nepal floods
Article Text:
Tharoor said he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Thursday said that he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district when he left for Kathmandu on Wednesday."A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Global warming and/or an earthquake in Tibet may have caused a large chunk of a glacier to break off and fall into the valley below, experts surmise," Tharoor said in a post on X.Tharoor added that the flooding had destroyed at least 19 motorable bridges and washed away around 40 km of the Betrawati–Rasuwagadhi highway. Eight operational hydropower projects were also reported to have sustained heavy damage.Tharoor said he supported the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance to Nepal, adding that the country would need substantial help in responding to the destruction.He also expressed concern over the loss of life and those still missing, including Indians affected by the disaster."I fully support the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance.Nepal needs all the help it can get. My heart goes out to the victims and their loved ones, who include large numbers of Indian tourists, including a hundred performing the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra. Prayers for the missing; may they be rescued soon," Tharoor said.The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet, according to authorities.The scale of destruction has hampered rescue operations, with Nepalese officials reporting that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometres (25 miles) of roads damaged.The Nepalese Army launched helicopter operations on Thursday morning, rescuing more than 100 people from flood-affected areas, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said. At least eight foreign nationals were also airlifted to Kathmandu, while army teams evacuated people trapped inside facilities associated with the Trishuli hydropower project.India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said five major groups, comprising around 288 Indian nationals, had been identified.“ The first group of 73 people who are working on the Trishuli-1 power project. Then, two separate groups of 37 and 49 nationals from Tamil Nadu, who traveled for Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Samrat and Fly Everest Travels. There is a group of 32 Indian nationals from West Bengal who traveled with the help of Samrat Travels in Timure, which is in Rasuwa district.”“Then, a group of 61 Indian nationals from different states and then a group of 33 Indian nationals from Kerala. These are five major groups who comprise, by and large, 288 people that we are talking about,” he added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and offered India’s assistance for rescue and relief operations.“India is prepared to provide Nepal with all possible types of humanitarian assistance,” PM Modi said, adding that Indian teams were coordinating rescue and relief efforts.The United Nations is also supporting the response, with agencies deploying personnel to assist local authorities. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric warned of a “massive humanitarian need” as rescue and relief operations continued.The disaster has also renewed concerns over the Himalayan region’s exposure to extreme weather events and glacial hazards, particularly in areas where difficult terrain and damaged infrastructure can complicate emergency response.
Article Summary: A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet. India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas.

NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Thursday met representatives of Reservation Hatao Andolan, which is protesting against caste-based reservation and demanding a complete overhaul at the national capital's Jantar Mantar.In a social media post on X, Nadda said that he met Harsh Dubey, Mrityunjay Pathak and Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan as per the pre-determined schedule, adding that another meeting will be held soon."Following the movement that took place at Jantar Mantar on August 21, cordial discussions were held, as per the pre-determined schedule, with Shri Harsh Dubey, Shri Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan, and Shri Mrityunjay Pathak, members of the team. In this connection, we will meet again soon," he said.However, Nadda did not give details of the meeting.Meanwhile, Harsh Dubey said that the meeting was an important step towards dialogue."Positive initiative for the welfare of all society today. Our team met with the honourable Shri JP Nadda Ji. During this time, there was a brief discussion with him regarding the demonstration that took place on August 21. This meeting is an important step towards dialogue.We will soon meet again with the honourable Nadda Ji and strive to move forward with a positive and just decision in the interest of all society," Dubey said."Our objective is not against any section, but rather to democratically and peacefully present our views for equal opportunities, a just system, and necessary reforms in the national interest. Further information and decisions regarding this will be officially communicated shortly," he added.Reservation Hatao Andolan is demanding that quotas in academics and employment should strictly be determined by income levels rather than social or caste identities. Additionally, the protesters advocated for a "one family, one reservation" policy and demanded the immediate withdrawal of the UGC's 2026 caste-equity directives.A large number of people gathered at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Friday to protest against caste-based reservation, following which the Delhi Police and Central Forces were deployed at the protest site to maintain law and order.Security personnel were seen present at Jantar Mantar as protesters assembled at the designated protest area. The police deployment was carried out as a precautionary measure amid the large gathering.Reservation Hatao Andolan (RHA) is an official Instagram page with 5.6 million followers. The platform rapidly gained traction by adopting the protest-mobilisation tactics of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and has now called for a physical protest against the reservation system.
Article Summary: Union minister JP Nadda on Thursday met representatives of Reservation Hatao Andolan. Protesters are protesting against caste-based reservation and demanding a complete overhaul at Jantar Mantar. Harsh Dubey, Mrityunjay Pathak and Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan met with the minister.

Water rose 30 feet and at least 160 people were killed, while hundreds of others, including scores of Kailash Mansar-ovar pilgrims from India, remained missing after a flash flood and mudslide of unprecedented scale in Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers tore through a part of Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday morning. It swept away settlements, hydropower units and the pilgrim route.Nepal Police put the toll at 157, while Chinese authorities reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Tibet’s Gyirong county. Nepal Police said 579 others — 466 foreigners from 28 countries and 113 Nepalis — remained untraced, including at least 133 Indians. Among the missing were at least 37 NRIs. Frighteningly, as many as 33 bodies were found 150km downstream at Chitwan, showing how far the dea-dly waters carried victims.Among the missing foreigners were 54 Americans, 34 Australians, 33 Britons, 24 Canadians, 19 Malaysians and 8 Koreans.Many were Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims, with nearly 400 of them, including the Indians, preparing to cross the Nepal-Tibet border or travelling through the region when the flood struck.Rescue personnel battled poor weather, mud, washed-out roads and high river levels even as authorities moved families from vulnerable settlements to safer locations.Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal told parliament that 29 police personnel and 44 soldiers remained untraced after floodwaters swept away their barracks in Rasuwa, while customs officials, hydropower workers and other employees stationed near the border were also missing. At the 20MW Langtang Khola Hydropower Project, dozens of workers are out of contact. The torrent also swept away or inundated security posts, customs facilities, banks and other establishments along the river corridor. Nepal PM Shah appealed for patience and unity as the Nepali Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force deployed helicopters, drones, boats and ground teams for search-and-rescue operations.Across the border, floods and mudslides severed several roads, communications and electricity around the (dry) Gyirong port, a key Nepal-Tibet crossing used by Kailash-Mansarovar pilgrims. Chinese president Xi Jinping called for “all-out efforts to search and rescue people who are missing”.The flood destroyed critical infrastructure across northern and central Nepal, with preliminary govt estimates showing at least 19 bridges and around 40 km of roads damaged or washed away; 13 hydropower projects were hit, and around 200 trucks were lost. The Nepal govt declared the worst-affected areas disaster-hit zones for the next 3 months and ordered authorities to provide free treatment to the injured.
Article Summary: Nepal Police put the toll at 157, while Chinese authorities reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Tibet’s Gyirong county. Nepal Police said 579 others — 466 foreigners from 28 countries and 113 Nepalis — remained untraced, including at least 133 Indians. Among the missing foreigners were 54 Americans, 34 Australians, 33 Britons, 24 Canadians, 19 Malaysians and 8 Koreans.

Article Title: Day after Farooq dare, Srinagar MP Mehdi decides to quit Lok Sabha, NC over Article 370
Article Text:
NC MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi announces resignation from Lok Sabha and party after Farooq Abdullah's public dare to contest on his own.

SRINAGAR: National Conference’s Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi announced Friday that he would resign from both Lok Sabha and the party, taking up patriarch Farooq Abdullah’s public dare to quit and contest an election on his own instead of criticising the brass repeatedly over its alleged dilution of the campaign for restoration of Article 370.Mehdi said he would formally send his resignation to LS Speaker Om Birla on Nov 3, coinciding with the 26th death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, who was killed by terrorists.In a letter to Farooq, who remains NC president, Mehdi flagged what he sees as a dichotomy in the party’s stand on constitutional guarantees for the region. “I remember that you were the chief minister of the very assembly that passed the autonomy resolution. That, too, must have required courage. Why, then, has the mere mention of constitutional guarantees for Jammu & Kashmir now become so offensive that you felt compelled to publicly demand my resignation?”The MP described Article 370, struck off on Aug 5, 2019, as part of the decision to revoke J&K’s special status, as “shorthand for the struggle to restore the dignity, honour, constitutional guarantees and liberties” of Kashmiris.“Nearly 65% of J&K’s population is young, and their future is increasingly uncertain, with no jobs and opportunities. Our land is up for grabs. Our resources benefit everybody but us. Our religious rights, traditions and language face constant pressure,” Mehdi wrote.The MP has been increasingly critical of CM Omar Abdullah and NC for allegedly narrowing their fight to statehood and business rules for governance.Although a member of the party’s working committee, he hasn’t been part of crucial meetings.His rift with the party deepened after Dec 23, 2024, when he led a large student protest outside Omar’s Gupkar residence against the UT’s reservation policy. Omar engaged five student representatives in a long discussion but ignored Mehdi.Earlier this week, Farooq said Mehdi would not have won the parliamentary election without NC and accused him of trying to project himself as a powerful votary of Article 370 while being “on the wrong path”.
Article Summary: National Conference’s Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi announced Friday that he would resign from both Lok Sabha and the party. Mehdi said he would formally send his resignation to LS Speaker Om Birla on Nov 3, coinciding with the 26th death anniversary of Aga Syed Mehdi.

Article Title: Pakistani drone detected in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch, security forces put LoC sector on high alert
Article Text:

Security forces along the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir have been put on high alert after fresh aerial activity originating from across the border was detected in the Poonch district.According to inputs from Army sources cited by news agency ANI, an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) from Pakistan was detected at around 8:05 pm on Friday.The drone was spotted hovering over the general area of Behrooti village in the Balakote area of Poonch's Mendhar sector, which falls under the operational area of responsibility of the 22 Jammu and Kashmir Rifles (22 JAK RIF).Military personnel tracked the UAV as it manoeuvred towards the Mangalnar-Dabrote side near the border before returning to Pakistan.Alert troops immediately logged the intrusion, following which the entire forward sector was placed under tight aerial and ground surveillance.Security forces launched the search operation at first light on Saturday in adjoining forward areas to check for any possible dropping of contraband or arms.Monitoring along the border remains active, and further official updates are awaited.The latest incident comes amid heightened security concerns along the India-Pakistan border and follows other suspected drone sightings reported in Jammu and Kashmir in recent weeks.Earlier this month, security forces launched a search operation after a suspected Pakistani drone was spotted over forward villages along the International Border in Jammu and Kashmir's Kathua district.The BSF and Jammu and Kashmir Police conducted searches to ensure that no weapons, explosives or other material had been dropped.A suspected Pakistani drone was also spotted in Rajouri's Sunderbani sector last month, after which security forces carried out a search operation but found nothing suspicious.Earlier in June, Army personnel opened fire after spotting a Pakistani drone over forward posts in the Balakote sector of Poonch, forcing it to retreat towards Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.Notably, the latest incident also comes days after an unusual increase in Turkish military transport flights to Pakistan raised concerns in Indian defence circles.Open-source flight trackers recorded a surge in Turkish C-130 Hercules and A400M aircraft flights between August 19 and 21, with the planes landing at Pakistani air bases, including Nur Khan, Masroor and Murid.There was speculation in defence circles that the flights may have carried military hardware, including unmanned aerial systems and air-defence equipment, although neither Pakistan nor Turkey officially confirmed the nature or cargo of the operations.Separately, security forces are carrying out massive search operations in the forested districts of Udhampur, Kathua and Rajouri following information about suspicious movement, according to news agency PTI.In Rajouri, another search operation was launched in Gaibas, Mithiyani, Mogla and Narla after villagers reported the movement of two suspected armed persons, believed to be terrorists.No contact with any suspected persons had been established so far, officials said.The latest incident in Poonch comes as security forces continue to maintain heightened surveillance along forward areas of Jammu and Kashmir.
Article Summary: Drone spotted hovering over Behrooti village in the Balakote area of Poonch's Mendhar sector. Military personnel tracked the UAV as it manoeuvred towards the Mangalnar-Dabrote side near the border before returning to Pakistan. Comes amid heightened security concerns along the India-Pakistan border.

Article Title: From Reds to NGOs: RSS weekly expands ‘dimagi Naxal’ label
Article Text:
‘Organiser’ termed NAC as marking the “classic takeover of the ‘dimagi Naxals’ of governance”

NEW DELHI: The RSS has joined the campaign against “dimagi Naxals” which PM Modi launched on Aug 15, with its affiliated weekly ‘Organiser’ arguing that the Sonia Gandhi-led National Advisory Council (NAC) under UPA allowed Maoist-influenced thinking to enter policymaking.In an editorial, ‘Organiser’ termed NAC as marking the “classic takeover of the ‘dimagi Naxals’ of governance”. It said, “As the armed rebellion has failed miserably, the dimagi variant has taken charge.” The editorial added penetrating bureaucracy, policy machinery, legal system, academia, media and NGOs formed part of this “revolutionary strategy”.The weekly stopped short of accusing Sonia or Congress brass of links with Maoists, directing its criticism at NAC and the ideological influence the body brought into governance.It distinguishes “dimagi Naxals” from ordinary agitators or reform groups, acknowledging issues such as education and climate change can be genuine while alleging such concerns may be appropriated by an ideological core. In his I-Day speech, PM said armed Naxalism was nearing its end but people subscribing to the ideology who entered govt panels as advisers were still looking to create violence and anarchy.That reference also appeared to recall UPA-era controversies involving human rights activist Binayak Sen.Sen, arrested in 2007, was nominated to the Planning Commission steering committee on health in 2011.The govt has sought to draw a boundary around the expression. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said Modi was not accusing opposition netas or parties, but referring to those supporting Maoists, who reject Constitution and back separatism.Set up in 2004 and chaired by Sonia Gandhi with cabinet-rank status, NAC brought activists, academics and experts into policymaking and played an important role in measures such as RTI and MGNREGA.
Article Summary: The RSS has joined the campaign against ‘dimagi Naxals’ which PM Modi launched on Aug 15. RSS’s affiliated weekly ‘Organiser’ argues that the Sonia Gandhi-led National Advisory Council (NAC) under UPA allowed Maoist-influenced thinking to enter policymaking.

Article Title: Have you done the truth test?
Article Text:
Thiruvalluvar captures the essence of this discipline in Kural 423:Epporul yaaryaarvaai ketpinum ApporulMeipporul kaanbadhu arivu.“Wisdom is to discover the truth in whatever is heard, irrespective of who says it.”Valluvar does not ask us to accept or reject an idea based on the identity of the speaker. He asks us to examine the truth within the statement.Iago’s words were believed because of who he appeared to be. Valluvar asks us to reverse that instinct: not “Who said this?” but “Is this true?”Truth is not measured by who speaks, but by what withstands examination.

Someone tells you that your closest friend has been speaking against you. At work, you hear that a colleague has spoiled your chances of a promotion. What do you do? Do you believe the person who told you, simply because you consider that person honest and dependable? Or do you pause and ask: How do I know if this is true?Shakespeare gave us a tragic answer to this question in ‘Othello’. Iago manipulates Othello by describing how his wife Desdemona’s handkerchief was with his friend Cassio, driving Othello into a jealous rage. The tragedy was not merely that Iago lied. It was that Othello failed to examine. He ended up killing Desdemona.How, then, does one ascertain truth? Is there a method by which we can distinguish what is real from what is merely reported, assumed or imagined?Interestingly, our ancestors believed in measuring everything accurately. Whether it was a piece of cloth or the jaggery needed for a pot of payasam, things had to be measured. In Tamil, there is a term, ‘Alavai iyal’ — the science of measurement. But measurement was not confined to physical objects. Indian philosophy also explored ways of measuring truth itself.These methods are called ‘pramanams’, means by which valid knowledge about what is true is obtained. Traditionally, six pramanams are described.The first is ‘pratyaksha’, or ‘kaatchi alavai’ — knowledge through direct perception using any of the senses. I smell gas and conclude there is a leak.The second is ‘anumana’, or ‘karuthal alavai’ — inference. I see smoke rising from a distance and infer that there must be a fire.The third is ‘agama pramanam’ or ‘urai alavai’ — knowledge obtained through texts.The fourth is ‘upamana pramanam’ or ‘uvamai alavai’ — knowledge through comparison. Understanding the unknown through knowledge about the known.The fifth is ‘arthapatti’ or ‘porul alavai’ — postulation from circumstances. The house is unusually quiet. We may infer that there was a big fight and now everybody is silent. It is not direct knowledge, but a conclusion drawn from circumstances.The sixth is ‘anupalabdhi’ or ‘inmai alavai’, knowledge through non-perception or absence. If someone claims to have seen a polar bear in Antarctica, the claim can be rejected because polar bears are native to the Arctic.These are not merely philosophical categories, but disciplines for the journey towards truth. Without them, our minds can easily become prisoners of assumptions and biases.Bias is perhaps our first obstacle. If someone we admire says something, we are inclined to accept it. If someone we dislike says the same thing, we may instinctively reject it. In both cases, we judge the statement by the person rather than examining its truth.The pramanas provide a framework to go beyond what our eyes can see without letting imagination outrun reason. They help us test assumptions, examine evidence and separate fact from illusion.
Article Summary: Valluvar does not ask us to accept or reject an idea based on the identity of the speaker. He asks us to examine the truth within the statement. In Tamil, there is a term, ‘Alavai iyal’ — the science of measurement.

Article Title: 'NC’s position no different from BJP': Srinagar MP accepts Farooq Abdullah's challenge, likely to resign

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir National Conference's estranged MP from Srinagar Aga Ruhullah Mehdi on Friday said he will resign from Parliament, accusing party chief Farooq Abdullah and the NC leadership of abandoning the fight for restoration of Article 370 , despite securing a mandate on the issue in the 2024 Assembly elections.In a two-page letter to Abdullah, Mehdi sought answers over the party's change in its position on Article 370. His remarks came after Abdullah asked him to seek a fresh mandate for opposing the party line.Referring to Abdullah's recent statement urging Kashmiris to become self-reliant instead of seeking economic concessions from the Centre, Mehdi said the remarks reflected his own frustration with being expected to adopt a “posture of supplication” before the BJP.He questioned why the party leadership objected when he raised similar concerns over Jammu and Kashmir's constitutional rights.“The uncomfortable truth is that we are not even 'begging' for Article 370; we are 'begging' for statehood – a right the Supreme Court itself has recognised,” Mehdi said, arguing that the NC's current position had become indistinguishable from that of BJP.The letter came amid reports that Mehdi is likely to resign from the Lok Sabha on November 3, the death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, who was assassinated in an IED blast on November 3, 2000.Mehdi warned that treating statehood as the limit of political aspirations could legitimise the constitutional changes made in August 2019 and weaken protections for Jammu and Kashmir's land, culture and environment.He also questioned NC's decision to move away from its 2024 assembly election promise of restoring Articles 370 and 35A.“Today, we conveniently argue that the very regime which abrogated Article 370 will never restore it… That would have been a fair argument. But the BJP was also in power when we drafted our 2024 manifesto. So, why did we include the restoration of Article 370 in our manifesto?” he asked.“Were we making promises we knew we could not keep or perhaps never truly intended to keep? Did we invoke the wound inflicted on the people of Jammu and Kashmir in August 2019 merely to derive political mileage, only to conveniently forget our promises after government formation?” he added.Pointing out that nearly 65 per cent of Jammu and Kashmir's population is young, Mehdi said their future was “increasingly uncertain” due to a lack of jobs and opportunities.“Our land is up for grabs. Our resources benefit everybody but us. Our religious rights, traditions, and language face constant pressure. Our environment is being ravaged by illegal deforestation, mining, and construction in ecologically fragile zones,” the Srinagar MP said.He said elected representatives must fight “this constant degradation and dehumanisation” instead of limiting public aspirations to what the BJP was willing to concede.“It is to ensure that the extraordinary and deeply consequential events of August 2019 do not become the new political normal and to recognise that restoration of statehood cannot be treated as an adequate substitute for what was taken away,” Mehdi said."Rest assured, the resignation will come. It would have come even without you asking, but before that must come accountability," he added.The letter comes at a time when reports suggest that the Srinagar MP is likely to resign from the Lok Sabha on November 3, coinciding with the death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, who was assassinated by terrorists in an IED blast on November 3, 2000.
Article Summary: National Conference's estranged MP from Srinagar Aga Ruhullah Mehdi said he will resign from Parliament. He accused party chief Farooq Abdullah and the NC leadership of abandoning the fight for restoration of Article 370. His remarks came after Abdullah asked him to seek a fresh mandate for opposing the party line.

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Friday received 21 Tamil Nadu pilgrims after they were rescued from the floods in Nepal.In a social media post on X, Jaishankar said that he was moved after hearing their experience and thanked Nepal government and army for their rescue effort."Received a group of 21 pilgrims from Tamil Nadu who were rescued from the floods in Nepal," Jaishankar said."Was moved to hear their experience first hand. Thank the Nepali Army and Government for this rescue effort. Appreciate Embassy of India, Kathmandu’s facilitation of their smooth return to India," he added.While talking to reporters at Delhi airport, Jaishankar also said that the government is focused on contacting all the Indians who are stranded in Nepal."So I want to say right now we are still very much focused on contacting all the Indians who are there. NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister P Viswanathan on Friday dismissed calls to project TVK chief Vijay C Joseph as the INDIA bloc’s prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha polls, asserting that Rahul Gandhi is the “definitive” choice.“As Congress leaders, we are very clear. Our beloved leader and leader of the opposition, Rahul Gandhi, is the INDIA bloc’s prime ministerial candidate for 2029,” Viswanathan said.His remarks came after several TVK leaders pushed for Vijay to be projected as a prime ministerial candidate for 2029 Lok Sabha polls , drawing sharp reaction from Congress.TVK leaders, including KA Sengottaiyan and D Sarathkumar, have compared Vijay with former Tamil Nadu chief ministers MGR and Jayalalithaa, claiming he would not only rule Tamil Nadu but also lead the country in the future.TVK legislator Kallanai, who organised an event marking the party’s 100 days in office, said people had immense faith in Vijay’s leadership. He expressed confidence that Vijay would eventually lead the country and hoist the national flag at the Red Fort as a representative of the Tamil people, news agency PTI reported.Meanwhile, Congress MP Karti Chidambaram said that while party workers may have deep admiration for their leader, national leadership ultimately depends on securing the numbers required to form a government.“I fully accept that they have great love, affection, expectation, and admiration for their party leadership. This is their party. What they say within their party makes no difference to the public discourse. In public discourse, what you should ask about is policy and the law. Their wishes within a party make no difference to me,” Chidambaram told reporters, according to ANI.He said every political party has its own ambitions and aspirations, but any prime ministerial aspirant must ultimately have the numbers to command a majority in the Lok Sabha.“Every party has dreams, ambitions, and desires. One cannot pass laws to stop that. Everyone expresses their own wishes and talks about their favourite leader in their party. But we know what the political reality is. There are 543 constituencies," Chidambaram said.According to the Constitution, the leader of whichever alliance wins 272 constituencies, or whichever party wins, will be the Prime Minister of India. Anyone who achieves that number can become the Prime Minister, individually or collectively. You and I both know what that political reality is,” he added.

A survivor of the ambush that killed four members of the Liangmai Naga community in Manipur's Kangpokpi district on Friday has recalled how armed attackers, dressed in full camouflage uniforms, opened fire on their vehicle in a forested area.Forty-four-year-old Gaikamang Ringkangmai, who sustained a bullet injury to his left arm, was rescued by security forces from the ambush site and admitted to Senapati district hospital.Recalling the attack, Ringkangmai said as quoted by news agency PTI, "I am from Makui village. Yesterday, there were six of us in a vehicle. We frequently travelled by that route. We were going to Senapati district when we were ambushed by militants. Four of our colleagues died on the spot, while two of us escaped."He said he was injured during the firing but managed to flee the vehicle and take shelter in nearby bushes."I received bullet injuries on my arm but jumped from the vehicle and ran to hide in the bushes," he added.Describing the attackers, Ringkangmai claimed they were positioned in pairs and wore full camouflage uniforms. "They had red ribbons tied to the top of their rifles, from which they continued firing," he added.The other person who survived the ambush has been identified as Japou MK.The attack took place around 8.30 am on Thursday in an isolated, forested stretch between Makui Ashang and Thabamba Naga villages in Kangpokpi district. According to reports, the armed attackers targeted the vehicle carrying the group, killing four people on the spot and injuring another.The deceased have been identified as Tadsongbou Ringkangmai, founder and principal of a private school; M Wijunamai; Anil Wijunamai; and Wisobou Charenamai, chairman of the Chawangkining Village Authority. All six people travelling in the vehicle belonged to the Liangmai Naga community.The killings have triggered demands for justice from the Naga community, even as authorities move to identify and apprehend those responsible.W Charenamei, younger brother of deceased Wisobou Charenamai, said the family and community were not seeking retaliation."We don’t seek any revenge against the militants. We just want the facts to be established and swift justice for our murdered brothers."Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh has directed security officials to arrest those involved in the killings and initiate action against them.The United Naga Council (UNC), the apex Naga body in Manipur, has alleged that two Kuki militant outfits, the Kuki National Front (P) and Kuki Revolutionary Army (KRA), were behind the ambush.
Article Summary: Manipur ambush survivor says attackers wore camouflage uniforms. Four members of Liangmai Naga community killed in ambush in Kangpokpi district. The United Naga Council (UNC) has alleged that two Kuki militant outfits were behind the ambush.

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police have arrested a city-based couple who allegedly worked for Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) through social media since 2024, officials said on Friday.The accused have been identified as Md Sahil and his wife, Sameera.According to Delhi Police's Special Cell, which investigated the case and made the arrests, the accused couple provided logistical support to Pakistan-based handlers and procured Indian SIM cards, which were sent to Pakistan via Dubai for use by Pakistani intelligence operatives.The couple allegedly sent eight Indian SIM cards to Pakistan during 2024 and 2025 and received around Rs 30,000 in return.The probe began after the Special Cell received information about an ISI-backed Pakistani intelligence operatives network operating in the Delhi-NCR region. The network recruited locals to procure SIM cards, which were sent to Pakistan through Dubai. WhatsApp accounts were then activated using the Indian numbers and used by Pakistani operatives to enter Indian WhatsApp groups and gather sensitive information, police said.The investigation led to Sahil’s arrest. Forensic analysis of his phone revealed conversations with Pakistani agents. During interrogation, Sahil told investigators that he was introduced to a Pakistani agent on Instagram in 2024 through Sameera, whom he later married. The agent subsequently connected the couple with a Pakistani intelligence operative, who recruited them in exchange for financial incentives.Sahil was also tasked with recruiting people to conduct reconnaissance of cantonment areas and obtain details about Army personnel facing court-martial proceedings, according to the Special Cell.Sameera was later arrested for her role in providing Indian SIM cards to Pakistani entities. Forensic examination of both accused’s phones revealed WhatsApp conversations with their Pakistani handlers.Two mobile phones used in the operation were recovered. Investigators are now examining the network’s structure, modus operandi and links with local operatives and sleeper cells.
Article Summary: Delhi Police have arrested a city-based couple who allegedly worked for Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) through social media since 2024. The accused have been identified as Md Sahil and his wife, Sameera. The couple allegedly sent eight Indian SIM cards to Pakistan during 2024 and 2025 and received around Rs 30,000 in return.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party founder Dipke has called for a “complete overhaul” of the country's education system following the death of 31-year-old IIT Delhi MSc Physics student Rishikesh Kumar. Dipke said that students need an environment where they feel “supported, heard and hopeful about their future”.In a post on X, Dipke wrote: “IITs, considered among the best educational institutions in our country, have witnessed 65 student suicides in the last five years. If this is the situation at our best institutions, imagine the state of the rest. We need a complete overhaul of our education system, one that creates an environment where students feel supported, heard and hopeful about their future, rather than leaving them isolated, overwhelmed and struggling in silence. ”Rishikesh died on August 22 after falling from the sixth floor of the Lecture Hall Complex. Police have said no suicide note was recovered and the circumstances surrounding his death are being investigated.Dipke's remarks came as IIT Delhi moved to constitute a final external inquiry committee to investigate the circumstances surrounding Rishikesh's death.The committee will be headed by retired Delhi high court judge Justice Mukta Gupta and will include Professor Pratap Sharan, head of the Department of Psychiatry at AIIMS New Delhi, four student representatives and IIT Delhi Registrar, who will serve as secretary and convenor, sources told ANI.The panel will interact with students, faculty members and administrative officials, review existing protocols and processes, and recommend measures to strengthen student support systems. It has been asked to submit its report within two weeks.The committee was reconstituted after former Uttarakhand DGP Ashok Kumar, who had initially been proposed as chairperson, recused himself citing prior commitments. Students had earlier demanded that the inquiry be headed by a former High Court judge.The earlier committee was announced by IIT Delhi Director Professor Rangan Banerjee after protests over Rishikesh's death. Students had demanded an independent probe, the resignation of the Dean of Student Welfare and financial assistance for his family.Rishikesh joined IIT Delhi in July 2025 and was staying in a campus hostel. The institute said he had received counselling and medical treatment after concerns were raised by fellow students following Holi celebrations. His requests to withdraw from the second and third semesters were also approved.
Article Summary: Dipke's remarks came as IIT Delhi moved to constitute a final external inquiry committee to investigate the circumstances surrounding Rishikesh's death. The committee will be headed by retired Delhi high court judge Justice Mukta Gupta and will include Professor Pratap Sharan.

JAMMU: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&K’s Samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated in the area and satellite communication was detected around 1pm Tuesday.“The reported activation of Iridium satellite sets raised suspicion among security agencies, following which a combined team of the Army, police, and personnel from other forces rushed to Sumb’s Makoli village and initiated extensive searches in and around the area,” an official said Wednesday.“Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to.The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found. Security was tightened along all routes leading to Sumb, with J&K Police and Village Defence Guards maintaining strict vigil, officials said.The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective as the route runs along the Basantar river and leads towards the India-Pakistan international border. Due to its proximity to the border, Samba district is a hotbed of terrorist activities. It serves as a gateway district for ultras heading towards Kashmir Valley via the upper reaches of Samba-Udhampur-Doda-Kishtwar.
Article Summary: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&K’s Samba district. Article Title: SC judge complains against Rajasthan acting CJ; CJI Surya Kant seeks response

NEW DELHI: Responding to letters written by SC judge Sandeep Mehta complaining against Rajasthan high court acting chief justice (ACJ) Sanjeev Prakash Sharma and seeking his transfer outside the state, CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response.Justice Mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring Sept 26, and appointment of a regular chief justice. Justice Mehta also complained as to why CJI Kant had not acted on his fervent pleas.Justice Mehta, who also hails from Rajasthan HC, has accused Justice Sharma of lacking in leadership qualities and alleged there was maladministration and malpractice on both judicial and administrative sides of HC.CJI Kant told TOI that the matter can be resolved only as per the established mechanism. “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media,” he said. He also released a public statement Wednesday decrying the attempt to hold a public trial over allegations made by one judge against another.Contents of the letters cannot be adjudicated in public domain and that judge concerned must be given a fair opportunity to place his response before any conclusion is reached.The fact that allegations have been made, therefore, cannot by itself be treated as a finding against the judge,” CJI Surya Kant’s statement said.The established mechanism for inquiring into allegations of an Supreme Court or High Court judge is the constitution of an in-house committee — comprising judges — by the Chief Justice of India, if he finds the response of the judge accused of misdemeanour or corrupt practices unsatisfactory and feels the charges are serious enough to warrant a deeper probe.CJI Kant, who is on a three-day official visit to Germany, also told TOI that he has already sought a response from Justice Sharma following the letters from Justice Mehta, who has alleged that there is “clear evidence of favouritism” by Justice Sharma. Justice Mehta’s complaints are being examined, CJI Surya Kant said.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response. Justice Mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring Sept 26. CJI Kant: “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media’

Article Title: ‘Biggest deal in history’: Trump says US to control 65 billion barrels of Venezuela oil
Article Text:
Trump had discussed bringing US oil companies back to Venezuela shortly after Maduro was removed.

US President Donald Trump on Friday announced what he described as an agreement with Venezuela that would give the US control over 65 billion barrels of the South American country's oil reserves.Trump said the deal was negotiated by Secretary of State Marco Rubio , Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez. He announced the agreement in a social media post.“The United States of America has just entered into an Agreement with the Country of Venezuela on, THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY!” Trump wrote.The announcement comes almost nine months after the US military, acting on Trump's orders, carried out an operation to capture Venezuela's President Nicolás Maduro. Maduro was taken to the US to face federal charges related to narcoterrorism and drug trafficking.The oil agreement also comes at a difficult time for Trump domestically, with high petrol prices putting pressure on his administration. The war in Iran has now reached its six-month mark with no clear end in sight, adding to concerns over energy supplies.The US has already been using its strategic petroleum reserves to help deal with energy pressures.The stockpile fell below 300 million barrels in early August, a drop of more than 100 million barrels since the beginning of 2026.Trump had discussed bringing US oil companies back to Venezuela shortly after Maduro was removed from power in January. He has also accused Venezuela of taking US oil after former President Hugo Chávez nationalised hundreds of foreign-owned assets, including those belonging to American oil companies.Venezuela has an estimated 303 billion barrels of crude oil reserves, making it one of the world's largest holders of oil. According to the US Energy Information Administration, this represents around 17% of global oil reserves.Much of Venezuela's oil is already mapped and known, meaning companies do not have to search extensively for new deposits. However, the country has struggled to turn those reserves into production because its oil infrastructure has deteriorated badly.As a result, Venezuela currently produces only around 1% of the world's oil despite holding such a large share of global reserves.
Article Summary: Venezuela has an estimated 303 billion barrels of crude oil reserves, making it one of the world's largest holders of oil. According to the US Energy Information Administration, this represents around 17% of global oil reserves. The announcement comes almost nine months after the US military carried out an operation to capture Venezuela's President Nicolás Maduro.

Article Title: 18 rounds, 5 bullets: How Haryanvi singer Ankit Balyan who sang ‘Court Mein Goli Marenge’ was gunned down outside gym

Haryanvi singer Ankit Balyan was shot dead outside a gym in Shamli district.

LUCKNOW: Haryanvi singer and YouTuber Ankit Balyan, 32, was shot dead in a point-blank attack outside a gym in Shamli district on Wednesday evening, with preliminary information indicating that around 18 rounds were fired at him.The incident took place around 7 pm near Aryapuri Nala Patri in the City Kotwali area. Police said the attackers arrived on two motorcycles and opened fire as Balyan stepped out of the gym and headed towards his Scorpio SUV.Also read: Delhi model dies after being stabbed multiple times in abdomen According to police and eyewitness accounts, four assailants were allegedly waiting outside the gym. Balyan reportedly tried to shield himself by moving towards the co-driver's side of the SUV as a wall obstructed the driver's side.The attackers allegedly pulled open the vehicle door and fired repeatedly at close range. Five bullets reportedly struck Balyan in the head and abdomen, while three hit the front windshield of his SUV.Balyan was rushed to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival. The attackers fled the scene, and police teams reached the spot soon after.Additional director general of police, Meerut Zone, Bhanu Bhaskar, reached Shamli along with senior officers to oversee the investigation.Superintendent of Police M P Singh said teams had been formed to identify and arrest the assailants.Police are examining CCTV footage from the gym and surrounding areas to identify the attackers and establish the sequence of events. Officials are also looking into a possible link to Haryana and investigating the motive behind the killing.The murder triggered protests by Balyan's family members, supporters and villagers. Protesters blocked the Delhi-Muzaffarnagar Road, around 50 metres from the shooting site, demanding immediate arrests and strict action against the accused.The situation became emotional after Balyan's body was brought to the road. His mother was seen holding her son's head in her lap and pleading with people not to disturb him, saying, "Don't speak, my son is sleeping."Balyan, a resident of Bantikheda village in Shamli, had more than 3.66 lakh YouTube subscribers and was known for his Haryanvi songs and performances. His videos often featured SUVs and firearms. He was also known for the song "Bhari Court Mein Goli Marenge Meri Jaan."He had attracted attention during a roadshow in Shamli in 2023, following which an FIR was registered against him and several supporters for alleged violations. There was also speculation that he was preparing to enter district panchayat politics, although police and his associates had not officially confirmed whether this was linked to the killing.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav condemned the murder, alleging that the law-and-order situation in Uttar Pradesh had been reduced to "zero". He also demanded that the possibility of political rivalry be investigated.Yadav described reports of Balyan's mother mourning with her son's body in her lap as "heart-wrenching" and said members of the Jat community were demanding the immediate arrest of the attackers.Police said no arrests had been made till late Wednesday night and that the investigation was underway.
Article Summary: Haryanvi singer and YouTuber Ankit Balyan, 32, was shot dead in a point-blank attack. The incident took place outside a gym in Shamli district on Wednesday evening. Police said the attackers arrived on two motorcycles and opened fire.

NEW DELHI: A 21-year-old woman was found stabbed to death inside her home in west Delhi's Tilak Nagar on Wednesday evening, police said.The woman, identified as Muskan, a student and a model was alone at home when she was allegedly attacked. HYDERABAD: Three students from the Telugu states, including one from Nizamabad, were killed in a road accident in Florida after their car rammed into a tree.The three were reportedly on their way to their workplaces, where they worked part-time jobs, when the accident occurred on Interstate 95 in Brevard County.The driver and the front-seat passenger died on the spot, while the third student, N Rahul of Navipet in Nizamabad district, who was seated in the rear, died while undergoing treatment at hospital. Rahul’s family was informed about the accident at around 3 am on Wednesday.The other two deceased were identified as Subramanyam Chaturvedula and G Anil. They are not letting anyone go near him as the investigation is still ongoing. A Telugu association is helping us in the US, but we also hope the state govt steps in and ensures that my son’s body is brought back,” said Hari Babu, Rahul’s father.According to the family, Rahul had completed his master’s degree but stayed back in South Florida as he wanted to pursue a PhD.They said he was reluctant to return to India as he felt it would be difficult for him to return to the US due to a raft of changes being made to immigration laws.“He used to call us every other day. Article Title: "Erika was photographed over his bloody mic": Candace Owens fires another shot at Erika Kirk as Tyler Bowyer’s Lindsay Clancy post sparks outrage
Article Text:
Candace Owens (Image via Getty)

Candace Owens challenges Tyler Bowyer over Erika Kirk comparison

Erika Kirk and Lindsay Clancy controversy intensifies

Candace Owens has sharply pushed back against a post by Turning Point USA chief operating officer Tyler Bowyer, who compared the public treatment of Erika Kirk with the support shown to Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy during her murder trial. Owens argued that criticism of fundraising efforts for Clancy can exist alongside criticism of TPUSA’s handling of Charlie Kirk’s death, adding another tense chapter to her long-running clash with the organization.The dispute began after Bowyer used X to contrast the backlash faced by Erika Kirk with the financial support surrounding Clancy’s legal case.His post stated, “strangle your three kids while evading your mental illness: ONE MILLION DOLLARS”.He then wrote, “lose your husband & father of your children but carry an organization with millions of followers on your back that recruits & registers young Patriots: A LIFETIME OF HARASSMENT”.Owens reposted Bowyer’s comments but rejected the comparison. She pointed to the commercial and fundraising activity surrounding Erika after Charlie Kirk’s death and questioned whether TPUSA should be weighing in on Clancy’s case at all.“You guys sold 50,000 t-shirts at the “event of the century” as Erika walked out to sparklers. You raised 40 million in one night at Mar-A-Lago as Erika was photographed over his bloody mic. It’s possible to disagree with fundraisers for Lindsay Clancy and also think TPUSA should sit this one out entirely.”Her response is significant because Owens has repeatedly criticized Erika Kirk and Turning Point USA since Charlie Kirk was killed. Rather than treating the controversy as a simple argument over Clancy, Owens has continued to use public posts to challenge how TPUSA has responded to the aftermath of Charlie’s death.The comparison comes as Clancy faces three murder charges in Massachusetts over the deaths of her children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months. She has pleaded not guilty.The case has also raised difficult questions about mental illness and criminal responsibility. If convicted, Clancy could face life in prison without parole. A finding of not guilty because of a lack of criminal responsibility could instead result in commitment to a state mental health facility.Meanwhile, Owens has continued questioning Erika Kirk publicly on several fronts. She has criticized Erika’s interactions with journalist Brandy Zadrozny, challenged the privacy surrounding Charlie Kirk’s burial location and raised broader questions about the events following his death.Charlie Kirk, 31, was fatally shot on September 10, 2025, during a student question-and-answer event at Utah Valley University in Orem, according to the university’s account of the shooting. Tyler Robinson has been accused in the killing.The latest exchange shows that the conflict surrounding Charlie Kirk’s legacy is far from settled. Owens’ response has shifted attention back toward the conduct of TPUSA itself, while Bowyer’s original post sought to highlight what he described as a stark difference in public sympathy. With both sides continuing to speak publicly, the controversy is likely to remain a major point of discussion among Kirk supporters and Owens’ audience.
Article Summary: Candace Owens has sharply pushed back against a post by Turning Point USA chief operating officer Tyler Bowyer. Bowyer compared the public treatment of Erika Kirk with the support shown to Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy during her murder trial. Owens argued that criticism of fundraising efforts for Clancy can exist alongside criticism of TPUSA’s handling of Charlie Kirk's death.

Article Title: CCTV shows BJP MLA's daughter slapping cop at Karnataka temple
Article Text:
CCTV footage shows an altercation between an MLA's daughter and a police sub-inspector.





MANDYA: CCTV footage has emerged of an altercation between a police sub-inspector and the daughter of Tumakuru Rural BJP MLA B Suresh Gowda at a temple in Srirangapatna, days after the incident was reported.The footage shows Aishwarya, the MLA's daughter, in a heated exchange with PSI Savitha B Patil at Aarti Ukkada temple on August 12. During the argument, Aishwarya is seen using her phone and attempting to make a call before allegedly slapping the police officer.Savitha then appears to hit her back, following which other people at the spot intervene and separate the two.The incident occurred around 4.30pm during Bhima Amavasya celebrations and was reportedly triggered by a dispute over entry into the temple's sanctum sanctorum.Savitha, attached to the Mandya Women's Police Station, was deployed for crowd-control duty at the temple. According to her complaint, Aishwarya arrived with others and sought to enter the sanctum without waiting in the queue. When Savitha asked her to wait for a few minutes to avoid inconvenience to devotees, Aishwarya allegedly identified herself as the MLA's daughter and questioned why she was being stopped.The argument allegedly escalated, with Aishwarya abusing and slapping the PSI and threatening to affect her career. Savitha subsequently filed a complaint at Kyathanahalli police station.Police registered an FIR against Aishwarya under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for allegedly assaulting a public servant, causing simple hurt, intentional insult and criminal intimidation.Aishwarya has also filed a counter-complaint, alleging that the police officer abused her. Police said the allegations in the counter-complaint were being examined.Speaking to reporters, MLA Suresh Gowda apologised for his daughter's conduct if she was found to have made a mistake and said anyone at fault should face action under law. He said Aishwarya had gone to the temple with two young children and had requested permission to enter briefly as waiting in the queue could have caused difficulty for them.The MLA also said his daughter should have exercised restraint as a member of a political family and called for a departmental inquiry into the incident.Gowda further opposed VIP arrangements at temples, saying devotees should be treated equally and made to follow the same queue system to avoid inconvenience to the public and reduce pressure on police personnel.
Article Summary: CCTV footage shows Aishwarya, the MLA's daughter, in a heated exchange with PSI Savitha B Patil at a temple in Srirangapatna. The incident occurred around 4.30pm during Bhima Amavasya celebrations and was reportedly triggered by a dispute over entry into the temple's sanctum sanctorum.

Article Title: Dera chief Ram Rahim walks out of jail again, gets 21-day furlough in 17th temporary release
Article Text:
Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh has received another 21-day parole from jail.





ROHTAK: Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh walked out of Rohtak's high-security Sunaria jail early on Tuesday after being granted a 21-day furlough, marking his 17th temporary release from prison since his conviction in 2017.Ram Rahim, who is serving sentences in separate cases of rape and murder, left the jail at around 6.00am amid security arrangements. As per the information he has left for Sirsa based Dera headquarters. The latest furlough comes less than two months after he returned to Sunaria jail on June 26 on completion of a 30-day parole.The Ram Rahim was lodged in Sunaria jail in August 2017 after being convicted in the rape case involving two female devotees .He was subsequently convicted in other cases, including the murder of Sirsa-based journalist Ram Chander Chhatrapati.With Tuesday's release, Ram Rahim has now been granted parole or furlough on 17 occasions during his imprisonment. His repeated temporary releases have frequently triggered questions and criticism, particularly over the frequency of the relief granted to a convict serving sentences in serious criminal cases.Earlier this year, Ram Rahim was granted 40 days of parole in January. He was again released on a 30-day parole in May and returned to the Rohtak jail on June 26 after completing the period of his temporary release.The latest 21-day furlough once again brings the controversial Dera chief out of jail.His release is also being linked with Punjab politics which would witness assembly elections next year in February.
Article Summary: Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh has been granted a 21-day furlough from Rohtak's high-security Sunaria jail. The release marks his 17th temporary release from prison since his conviction in 2017. He is serving sentences in separate cases of rape and murder.

Article Title: Tipu Sultan cutout video with Pakistan reference sparks row in Karnataka, 23-year-old arrested
Article Text:
This video featured a Tipu Sultan cutout with a song referencing Pakistan





CHIKKAMAGALURU: Chikkamagaluru Police arrested a 23-year-old man on Tuesday for allegedly circulating a video featuring a Tipu Sultan cutout with a song containing references to “Pakistan” and “Mujahid”, prompting heightened security in the district, police said.Superintendent of Police Jitendra Kumar Dayama clarified that the action was not related to the installation of the Tipu Sultan cutout itself.He said a similar cutout had been installed at Tipunagara at the same location, around the same time and with the same dimensions in previous years.According to Dayama, police had earlier told organisers they could continue with arrangements followed over the past five to 10 years, but would not permit any new cutouts or decorations.The issue surfaced around 5pm to 5.30pm when the cutout was used as the backdrop in a video and a song containing a word referring to “Pakistan” and “Mujahid” was added, the SP said.The video was later circulated through multiple social media accounts and came to the police’s attention, ANI reported.Police registered an FIR under Sections 196 and 299 and traced the account that first circulated the video, following which the 23-year-old local resident of Tipunagara was arrested and is being produced before a magistrate, Dayama said.He allegedly shared the video as his WhatsApp status, sent direct messages to some Instagram accounts and other individuals, and uploaded a reel on his Instagram account, police said.Police are also probing the role of others who may have viewed, shared or recirculated the content."We are still in the process of ascertaining their role. If someone else also with intention did the same, then we will definitely arrest them and produce them," Dayama said.The SP said police were also trying to identify the person who originally created the video. A request has been sent to Meta for the relevant IP address as part of efforts to trace the original account.Dayama said the situation in Chikkamagaluru remained peaceful and police had spoken to community leaders. He said action would be taken against anyone attempting to create disturbances.Police social media monitoring teams at both the district and police station levels were also closely monitoring the situation, he said.More than 300 Home Guards, four Karnataka State Reserve Police (KSRP) platoons and local police personnel have been deployed for security, Dayama said. The forces will continue to monitor the situation during the function and the upcoming procession."Everything is peaceful, everything is calm, and this function will go on," Dayama said.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Chikkamagaluru Police arrest a 23-year-old man for allegedly circulating a video featuring a Tipu Sultan cutout. The video featured a song containing references to “Pakistan” and “Mujahid’ The action was not related to the installation of the cutout itself.
